metadata.description: Test queries for evaluating RAG performance

expected.answer: The transformer is a neural network architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms.
Self-attention computes the relationship between different positions in a sequence.
BERT stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers.
GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer.
Attention allows the model to focus on relevant parts of the input.
Layer normalization normalizes inputs across features to stabilize training.
Masked language modeling trains by predicting masked tokens from context.
Encoder-decoder has an encoder for input and decoder for output generation.
Positional encoding adds position information to input embeddings.

queries.query: What is the scaled dot-product attention?

expected.answer: Scaled dot-product attention uses Q, K, V matrices with softmax.
Multi-head attention performs several attention operations in parallel.

queries.query: What is the role of feed-forward networks?

expected.answer: Feed-forward networks process each position separately with two linear layers.
Bidirectional processing considers both left and right context.
Next sentence prediction predicts if two sentences are consecutive.
Dropout randomly sets activations to zero during training to prevent overfitting.
Label smoothing uses soft targets instead of hard one-hot labels.
Warmup gradually increases learning rate from zero to target.
Transformers process all positions simultaneously unlike sequential models.

queries.query: What is the difference between encoder and decoder?

expected.answer: Encoder creates representations from input, decoder generates output.

queries.query: How many layers does the original transformer have?

expected.answer: The original transformer has 6 layers in encoder and decoder.

queries.query: What is the purpose of residual connections?

expected.answer: Residual connections help with gradient flow in deep networks.
Attention is computed as softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V.
Pre-training trains on large unlabeled data before task-specific fine-tuning.
Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model to a specific task.
Transfer learning applies knowledge from one task to another.

queries.query: What is the [CLS] token in BERT?

expected.answer: [CLS] is a special token used for classification output.

queries.query: What is the [SEP] token in BERT?

expected.answer: [SEP] separates sentences in BERT input.

queries.query: What is masked LM in BERT?

expected.answer: BERT randomly masks 15% of tokens and predicts them.
RoBERTa is an optimized version of BERT trained with better methodology.
Autoregressive generation predicts next token based on previous tokens.
Decoder-only uses causal attention for text generation.
Encoder-only uses bidirectional attention for understanding tasks.
Few-shot learning adapts to tasks with minimal examples.
In-context learning uses examples in the prompt without parameter updates.

queries.query: What is the embedding dimension in transformers?

expected.answer: The original transformer uses 512 dimensional embeddings.

queries.query: How many attention heads does the transformer use?

expected.answer: The original transformer uses 8 attention heads.
Feed-forward networks use 2048 hidden units.

queries.query: What is the vocabulary size of BERT?

expected.answer: BERT BASE uses 30522 vocabulary tokens.
Standard attention has quadratic complexity in sequence length.
Beam search keeps multiple hypotheses during generation.
Tokenization splits text into subword tokens.
WordPiece breaks words into subword units based on frequency.

queries.query: What is the benefit of larger models?

expected.answer: Larger models can learn more complex patterns and achieve better performance.
Emergent abilities appear in large models without explicit training.

queries.query: What is the training objective of BERT?

expected.answer: BERT uses masked language modeling and next sentence prediction.

queries.query: What is the training objective of GPT?

expected.answer: GPT uses causal language modeling to predict next token.

queries.query: What is the difference between BERT and GPT?

expected.answer: BERT is bidirectional encoder, GPT is unidirectional decoder.

queries.query: What is the maximum context window size of GPT-3?

expected.answer: GPT-3 has a maximum context window of 2048 tokens.
PEFT updates only a small subset of parameters.
Adapter tuning adds small layers that are trained while keeping base model fixed.
